sophia: Ran an nsys trace against the QA serving node and hit a bunch of CUPTI symbol errors, timeline is incomplete. Anyone seen this with mixed host/container CUDA versions?

mike: Can you paste the log?

sophia: ```
2026-03-17T14:07:12Z nsys[4321]: cuptiGetResult failed: CUPTI_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED (4)
Failed to register activity callbacks: cuptiActivityRegisterCallbacks returned 0x7
libcupti.so.12: undefined symbol: cuptiActivityRegister
```

ara: That looks like a libcupti version mismatch (undefined symbol usually means the runtime picked an older/newer libcupti than the headers nsight was built against). Which CUDA inside the container vs on host?

sophia: Host driver is 535.54, container image is based on cuda-12.2 runtime (toolkit files present in /usr/local/cuda-12.2). I tried setting LD_LIBRARY_PATH to the container's lib64 but nsys still logs the undefined symbol.

mike: nsys will often load libcupti from the host docker image or /usr/lib first. Two usual fixes: (1) LD_PRELOAD the container's libcupti.so into the nsys process, e.g. `LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/cuda-12.2/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so nsys profile ...` or (2) run `nsys --cuda-home=/usr/local/cuda-12.2 ...` to force the CUDA home. Which did you try?

sophia: Tried `--cuda-home` and LD_LIBRARY_PATH — still seeing the same undefined symbol because the host has an incompatible lib in /usr/lib that gets prioritized. I got a slightly different error when I LD_PRELOAD though: `cuptiActivityRegisterCallbacks returned 0x1` (CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER). Timeline still shows ~30% missing kernel events.

perf-bot: perf alert: profiling run 2026-03-17T14:07:12 produced incomplete timeline (missing kernel start/stop for ~30% of launches).

ara: Two more things to check: (A) /proc/sys/kernel/perf_event_paranoid — if it's >1 some perf counters are blocked and user-space tracing can be incomplete; (B) attaching permissions to PIDs in containers (seccomp/capabilities) — if the process isn't allowed to ptrace you'll lose events.

sophia: perf_event_paranoid was set to 2 on the node. I lowered it to 1 and re-ran — timeline improved but we still see missing CUDA activity on some worker PIDs and occasional `permission denied` when nsys tries to attach.

mike: For k8s pods the options are: run the profiling sidecar as privileged (not great), add CAP_SYS_PTRACE to the pod, or run the profiling inside the container as root and attach to child pids. We usually avoid privileged mounts. Another trick is to mount the host's /usr/local/cuda into the container so the lib paths match exactly.

ara: Also note there was a driver/driver-tooling bug affecting 535.86 and a couple of nearby versions where cupti activity enqueue calls were no-ops under heavy concurrency — NVIDIA released a hotfix in that release family. If you can capture `nvidia-smi -q`, `nsys --version` and md5sum of libcupti.so, it's good to open a kernel/driver bug with telemetry.

sophia: I'll collect versions and attach logs. Quick reproduce ask: does anyone have a minimal dockerfile + run flags that reliably reproduces the mismatch so we can share with NVIDIA?

mike: here's the snippet we used before (worked for us):
```
FROM nvidia/cuda:12.2-runtime
# install nsight that matches our host version
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y nsight-systems
# run with cap add to allow attach but not fully privileged
# docker run --rm --cap-add SYS_PTRACE --cap-add SYS_ADMIN -v /usr/local/cuda-12.2:/usr/local/cuda-12.2 your-image
```
This uses a host bind of /usr/local/cuda-12.2 so libcupti path is identical. We then start profiling with: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --cuda-home=/usr/local/cuda-12.2 ./start-server`

jasmin: tagging ops to patch nodes temporarily: @ops we might need a cluster-wide perf_event_paranoid drop + a one-off daemonset that mounts host /usr/local/cuda for reliable profiling. Are we ok with that for a short window?

sophia: @jasmin yes please — short window is fine. I'll upload the failing nsys trace and the md5sum of libcupti to the ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:

mike: one more note — if you see `CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED` it usually means the target process was started before CUPTI library was preloaded or the driver got in a weird state; restarting the process after ensuring correct libcupti in LD_PRELOAD usually clears that. Also consider trying perfetto on a dev node for a secondary trace (less intrusive).

ara: Agreed. I'll draft a short runbook for profiling infra: checks for libcupti path parity, perf_event_paranoid, necessary caps, and recommended nsys command-line flags. We'll drop it in the eng-runtime runbooks folder.

sophia: Perfect, thanks. I'll follow up in the ticket with the exact reproducer.
